The request: "Move the client sync regarding the finalization of the Meridian contract that ends at 3:30 pm to Room 4C. If there's none, just let me know."

So this is a "no target" probe with an escape clause ("If there's none, just let me know"). The correct behavior is to state that nothing matches and to change nothing.

So the solver acted on the decoy (wrote a PATCH to the decoy's location). The final answer also presents the decoy as a match ("Done — moved to Room 4C... It was the only client sync / Meridian event... so I assumed you meant this one").

Verdict: incorrect — acted on a non-target record (the decoy). The mechanical attribution also agrees: incorrect, exposed fact ['A:Event.end'].

This is a clear saw-mismatch-accepted.

Not an artifact: no ignored filter was involved (the q search was not ignored; the event came back legitimately; the decisive field start/end times were visible in the response and the solver did indeed look at them). The replica did not cause this.
